A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Null-TTA research and contain readable main text and supplementary material. Equations, tables, figures, and relocated sections can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-alignment experiments, qualitative examples, computational comparisons, and ablations, including SDXL and JPEG-compressibility results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds human preference results in Table 2 and comparisons across computational budgets in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The objective, embedding updates, annealing, candidate selection, and zeroth-order option remain unchanged. Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1 rename particle filtering as greedy search, but both versions already select the highest-reward candidate deterministically.

E1.justification: Both retain HPDv2 text-to-image evaluation, the same six qualitative scenarios, multi-objective alignment, and JPEG compressibility. SDXL and JPEG experiments move from the appendix into the main text. Human ratings introduce an evaluation procedure on existing HPDv2 coverage, rather than a new generation task or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new user study and budget analysis use existing comparators DAS and DNO; newly cited research is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct blind human-ranking protocol with 16 participants and 800 evaluations, reporting ranking frequencies and average rank. Figure 4 also varies DAS particle counts and DNO optimization steps beyond the previously reported default comparisons. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining existing generation settings.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 examines sensitivity of target-versus-held-out reward trade-offs to baseline computational budgets. The existing search-width, annealing, and regularization ablations are retained unchanged, moving from v1 Tables 3-5 to v2 Tables 6-8.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging experimental scores over three random seeds, without confidence intervals or error bars. Although v2 says humans 'statistically prefer' Null-TTA, it supplies no significance test or additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds an independent human-evaluation result set and baseline-budget curves. Table 2 reports first-place rates of 42.2% for Null-TTA, 30.9% for DNO, and 26.9% for DAS, with average ranks 1.81, 2.04, and 2.15 respectively. Figure 4 adds results under varied budgets. All original table values and the evidence in Figures 1-3 are retained.

T1.justification: The KL derivation, Gaussian assumptions, objectives, and zeroth-order estimator remain unchanged. The reverse-process mean newly displayed as v2 Equation 3 restates mathematics already present in v1 Equation 19; equation renumbering does not add theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about semantic-space alignment, distributional optimization without model-parameter updates, and strong target and cross-reward performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the human rankings as confirmation that reward gains translate into perceptual quality and extends its comparative interpretation to varying baseline budgets. It removes v1's short explanation that latent-space perturbations preserve valid generated samples. Existing over-optimization qualifications remain in the relocated ablation discussion.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies DAS's default 16 particles and DNO's default 100 optimization steps. Core hardware, optimizer, hyperparameter, scheduling, and JPEG-estimator details remain, mostly relocated. The explicit statement that SDXL reuses SD-v1.5 hyperparameters is omitted, without establishing an actual setting change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al.'s inference-time scaling work, discussed as Search over Paths, and Singhal et al.'s general framework for inference-time scaling and steering. These modestly broaden related-work coverage while preserving the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and supplement are substantially reorganized: implementation details and ablations move into the appendix, while SDXL and non-differentiable-reward experiments become main-text Sections 4.6-4.7. Terminology changes to greedy search, and the multi-objective discussion and several captions are shortened.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-ranking table and a three-panel budget figure, relocates five existing tables between the main text and appendix, and revises table-caption placement and experimental-page layout. The qualitative grid is resized; the underlying content of Figures 1-3 is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The human study and baseline-budget analysis strengthen validation of perceptual quality and comparison fairness while preserving existing evidence. Clearer greedy-search terminology also helps. The gain remains limited because the user study is sparsely documented, calls its 800 observations both pairs and evaluations, and reports no test supporting 'statistically prefer.'
